The search begins by checking the middle roll number in the current range. - If the middle roll number matches the required roll number, the search is successful. - If the required roll number is smaller, the same search process is repeated on the left half. - If the required roll number is larger, the search continues recursively on the right half. - If the search range becomes invalid (the left index becomes greater than the right index), the roll number is reported as not found. The following program implements this recursive binary search.

text: Which of the following statements about the program are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The recursive calls in Lines 11 and 14 reduce the search space in every recursive step.
The program can correctly perform binary search even if numbers is not sorted.
Line 5 compares the target with every element in the list.
The recursion stops either when the target is found (Line 8) or when the search range becomes invalid (Line 3).

explanation: - A: Correct. Each recursive call searches only one half of the remaining list. - B: Incorrect. Binary search requires the list to be sorted. - C: Incorrect. Line 5 only computes the middle index; it does not compare every element. - D: Correct. These are the two terminating conditions of the recursive binary search.
